# Pritiraj & Partners

> A governance and political strategy advisory practice in Bengaluru, India, founded by Pritiraj Brahma. The firm publishes The Pritiraj Review — evidence-led essays on Indian governance, state capacity, institutional design and fiscal federalism. Every figure in the Review is attributed to a named public source (PIB, RBI, CAG, NJDG, PRS, the Economic Survey, parliamentary replies).

The firm's position: politics is the promise, governance is the delivery. India's failures are failures of institutional design — tasks without owners, targets without deadlines, results nobody is required to publish — rather than failures of ambition or resource.

## Essays

- [Eight Hundred and Fifty Seats — What Delimitation Actually Decides](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/eight-hundred-and-fifty-seats-what-delimitation-actually-decides/): The Delimitation Bill, 2026 proposes a 850-member Lok Sabha with 272 seats reserved for women. The seat count is the least consequential thing about it.
- [The Arithmetic of Absence — Why Air India Is Losing a Market It Was Built to Lead](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-arithmetic-of-absence-why-air-india-is-losing-a-market-it-was-built-to-lead/): Air India's FY26 loss hit ₹22,238 crore as domestic share fell to 23.9%. A structured analysis of why the turnaround is stalling — and the correction required.
- [The Arithmetic That Should Alarm Us — India's Learning Crisis as a Solvency Problem](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/india-learning-crisis-the-arithmetic-that-should-alarm-us/): India enrols nearly every child and half leave unable to do grade-level mathematics. Why the learning crisis is now a fiscal question — and the five structural corrections it requires.
- [The Quiet Part of a Loud Victory — Symbol, Substance and the Exam Reform](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-quiet-part-of-a-loud-victory-dharmendra-pradhan-resignation/): The street took a scalp; the State had already rebuilt the system. Why the resignation of the Union Education Minister matters less than the five corrections that preceded it.
- [The Dashboard Problem — When Measurement Replaces Delivery](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-dashboard-problem/): India has more real-time government dashboards than any comparable state. Pendency, learning outcomes and delivery gaps have not moved with them. Visibility is not accountability.
- [The District Is Where the State Lives — The Tier India Refuses to Staff](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-district-is-where-the-state-lives/): India debates the Centre and the states endlessly and ignores the tier where governance actually succeeds or fails. The district runs at 19% IAS vacancy against a mandate that expands every year.
- [The CJP Protest — Ten Million Followers, One Unwinnable Demand](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/cjp-protest-unwinnable-demand/): Ten million followers in five days, and no institutional outcome. A strategist's diagnosis of five design errors — and the pivot that could still convert pressure into text.
- [The Forty-One Percent Illusion — State Finances After the Sixteenth Commission](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-forty-one-percent-illusion-state-finances-after-the-sixteenth-finance-commission/): The 16th Finance Commission held devolution at 41% and discontinued revenue deficit grants. Why a headline of continuity conceals the tightest state fiscal settlement in a decade.
- [The Certificate Is Not the Job — Why India Skills Millions and Employs Few](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-certificate-is-not-the-job/): PMKVY trained 13.7 million people in seven years and placed 18 per cent of them. The failure is not effort; it is a system built to count certificates instead of livelihoods.
- [The Campus Economy — India's Quietest Special Economic Zones](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-campus-economy-india-s-quietest-special-economic-zones/): Roughly 37% of notified SEZ land is in use. Meanwhile four university gates have built the concentrated capital, talent and IP pools that SEZ policy spent twenty years trying to engineer.
- [India's Demographic Clock — The Deadline Beneath Every Other Debate](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/india-s-demographic-clock/): A median age of 28 in an ageing world is India's greatest advantage and its deadline. The working-age share peaks in the 2040s; everything else is a question of what gets delivered before then.
- [Four Codes, Thirty-Six Rulebooks — The Labour Reform That Is Not Yet a Reform](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/four-codes-thirty-six-rulebooks-the-labour-reform-that-is-not-yet-a-reform/): Twenty-nine central labour laws were repealed on 21 November 2025. The central rules arrived on 8 May 2026. The states are where the reform is now decided.
- [The Northeast Is Not the Periphery — A Gateway That Is Not Yet Open](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-northeast-india-is-not-the-periphery/): Over ₹6 lakh crore committed in a decade, and the region's exports fell from $50.8m to $47.6m. The gateway framing is right; the execution gap is the whole problem.
- [The Last Mile Is the Whole Journey — What Seventy-One Farms Taught Me](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-last-mile-is-the-whole-journey/): Meghalaya imports 18,000 tonnes of pork a year while almost every household keeps pigs. The gap between those two facts is where Indian governance is actually decided.
- [The Tariff That Was Never Lawful — What India Conceded, and What It Should Learn](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-tariff-that-was-never-lawful-what-india-conceded-and-what-it-learned/): India negotiated relief from a 50% US tariff in February 2026. Three weeks later the US Supreme Court held the instrument behind it was never authorised. A lesson in negotiating against legal durability.
- [Cities Without Money — The Third Tier and the Capacity It Lacks](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/cities-without-money-the-third-tier-and-the-capacity-it-lacks/): India's cities produce roughly 60% of GDP and raise 0.6% of it. The Sixteenth Commission has now sent them ₹3.6 lakh crore against conditions most cannot yet meet.
- [The Thirty-Nine Percent Question — Health Spending and What It Buys](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-thirty-nine-percent-question-health-spending-and-what-it-buys/): Out-of-pocket health spending has fallen from 62.6% to around 39%. Public health spending sits at 1.8% of GDP against a 2.5% target. Both numbers describe the same unfinished settlement.
- [Who Regulates the Regulators](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/who-regulates-the-regulators/): India built independent regulators for its most important sectors and then left their appointments, budgets and accountability inside the ministries they were meant to check.
- [Airsheds Do Not Respect District Lines](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/airsheds-do-not-respect-district-lines/): India measures air pollution by city and manages it by municipality. The pollution arrives from a region several hundred kilometres wide. The mismatch is the whole problem.
- [The Missing Middle of Indian Enterprise](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-missing-middle-of-indian-enterprise/): Only 14% of India's MSMEs have formal credit, against a gap estimated between ₹25 and ₹30 lakh crore. Indian firms stay small because staying small is the rational response to the system around them.
- [The Discom Turnaround — and What It Does Not Yet Prove](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-discom-turnaround-and-what-it-does-not-yet-prove/): India's power distributors posted a collective profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 against accumulated losses of ₹6.47 lakh crore. A real turnaround, and a small one.
- [The Aquifer Is the Real Budget Constraint](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-aquifer-is-the-real-budget-constraint/): India extracts 247.22 BCM of groundwater a year — a quarter of the world's total. 730 assessment units are over-exploited. The binding constraint on Indian agriculture is not credit or price.
- [Five Crore Cases and the Arithmetic of Delay](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/five-crore-cases-and-the-arithmetic-of-delay/): India's courts carry more than 5 crore pending cases with roughly 14 judges per million people against a recommended 50. The backlog is not a moral failing; it is a capacity equation.
- [Citizens Who Move, Entitlements That Do Not](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/citizens-who-move-entitlements-that-do-not/): India built a portable ration card and stopped there. A migrant worker still cannot vote, see a doctor, enrol a child or claim a pension where they actually live.
- [The Half That Does Not Show Up — India's Female Participation Problem](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-half-that-does-not-show-up/): Female labour force participation has risen to 40%. Urban female participation sits near 25%, and 44.4% of women outside the workforce name care work as the reason. The constraint is not ambition.
- [The Title Is the Asset — Why Indian Land Cannot Be Used as Capital](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-title-is-the-asset/): India's land records are presumptive, not conclusive. A landholding you cannot prove you own is a landholding you cannot borrow against, sell cleanly, or defend in court.
- [Twenty Years After Prakash Singh — The Reform That Was Ordered and Never Delivered](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/twenty-years-after-prakash-singh/): The Supreme Court directed seven police reforms in 2006. Two decades on, forces run at roughly a fifth understrength and 86% of the state police is constabulary with one promotion in a career.
- [The Country That Stopped Counting Itself](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-country-that-stopped-counting-itself/): India's last census was in 2011. Every welfare list, every seat allocation and every per-capita figure in public use rests on a population that no longer exists.
- [The Capex Budget and the Capacity to Spend It](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-capex-budget-and-the-capacity-to-spend-it/): ₹12.22 lakh crore of capital expenditure against a 4.3% deficit. The Union Budget 2026-27 makes a coherent bet — and hands the binding constraint to the states.
- [The Largest Thing India Does Well](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-largest-thing-india-does-well/): India moves 64 crore people through a voting booth in six weeks without serious incident — the most impressive administrative act on earth. Everything surrounding that act is weaker than the act itself.
